title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
A network of private providers started to roll out a business continuity programme to support small and medium enterprises in the agriculture and agri-food sectors in facing the crisis. The programme aims to identify challenges in terms of business continuity, resilience and decent job retention, and then provide trainings, coaching and advisory services to help businesses become more resilient and retain jobs threatened by the ongoing crisis. A business plan competition for Lebanese and Syrian refugee entrepreneurs was organized in the presence of social partners. Over 650 entrepreneurs have been trained in the ILO's My first business training. Training beneficiaries then pitched their ideas in a business plan competition. A total of 42 projects were awarded in the first phase for which coaching and mentoring will be provided. A network of private providers, in close collaboration with constituents (chamber of commerce) introduced the "Improve your agri-business" training programme for small-holders farms. The training programme encompasses 6 topics and aims to support farmers in improving management of their farms for increased incomes and job creation. Value chain actors in horticulture (input suppliers) in collaboration with a public credit guarantee institution (Kafalat) adopted a new inclusive business model to enable smallholder farmers to upgrade to high-productivity greenhouse technologies. Actors started to implement an action plan to increase outreach to smallholder farmers and better inform them about the benefits of high-productivity modern greenhouse technologies, while also extending credit to farmers for the purchase of greenhouses. Extension of credit is made possible through credit guarantees offered by Kafalat. High-productivity greenhouse technologies should ultimately increase incomes of farmers and improve working conditions of workers. With the support of ILO and ITCILO, five freelance trainers were trained on business continuity. Trainers then assessed 20 selected enterprises and supported them in adapting their business plans. ILO provided wage subsidies and financial support for these enterprises as one of the immediate measures to support them retain their workers at the time of multiple crises.
ILO has trained trainers of its partners, the LEE experience, on its My first business (MFB) training programme. With financial support from ILO, the LEE experience rolled out the training programme and trained over 650 entrepreneurs ILO then supported the LEE experience in the organization of the business plan competition that aimed to select the best business ideas of entrepreneurs for further technical and financial support.
ILO revised the "Improve your Business" training programme adapting to the specific needs of smallholder farmers in Lebanon, and assessed the capacity of potential local partner organizations. ILO trained over 20 trainers from private sector and the chamber of commerce in the adapted "Improve your agri-business" training, and thus built the capacity ofpartner organizations to ensure sustainable roll-out of the training.
ILO conducted pilot trials with 12 farmers to showcase the benefits of high-productivity greenhouses and collect data on revenues of farmers and working conditions for farm workers. ILO in parallel conducted a survey that confirmed farmers' lack of knowledge of these benefits. ILO then presented the combined findings to selected value chain actors to convince them of the need of a more effective and inclusive outreach strategy, and assisted them in designing such a strategy. In parallel, ILO facilitated and financed an agreement between value chain actors and a public credit guarantee institution that enables suppliers to offer greenhouses on credit to farmers.
